title: Giftkönig Mithridates gegen Rom

title: Russia's giant new radar in Kaliningrad raises alarm in NATO
snippet: Russia is nearing completion of what experts think is a giant radar complex in Kaliningrad, capable of monitoring much of Europe. Experts warn the project could intensify the military standoff between Moscow and NATO.

title: Ethnic Germans in Kazakhstan face legacy of the Soviet Union
snippet: Kazakhstan is struggling to deal with the legacy of the Soviet dictatorship. Some 85 years ago, Stalin deported hundreds of thousands of people: Some 400,000 ethnic Germans living in the USSR were sent to Kazakhstan.

title: Germany's search for a nuclear waste site
snippet: Finland has become the first country with a final storage facility for nuclear waste. Germany is still searching for a site, while some countries have yet to start. Costs are expected to total many billions of euros.

title: Germany's Gen Z protests disrupted by violence on Saturday
snippet: Nationwide protests led by young people were largely peaceful throughout the day, but reports about looting and rioting in the evening, especially in Frankfurt, overshadowed the spirit of the demonstrations.

title: France: Hundreds arrested after nationwide protests
snippet: The French government says more than 1,000 people were arrested following nationwide protests on Saturday. Police and elite security forces were out in force across the country as clashes broke out.

title: ‘Gravestones are sinking into the ground’: Preserving Lithuania’s Jewish cemeteries
snippet: Before the Second World War, there were between 200 and 240 Jewish cemeteries in Lithuania. Most of them today stand neglected. The non-profit organisation MACEVA, the Litvak Cemetery Catalogue, has been working in Lithuania since 2011 to preserve this heritage.

title: Lithuania launches climate change map
snippet: Lithuania’s Hydrometeorological Service (Meteo LT) has launched a interactive website where users can view and download data on past climate conditions and projected changes up to 2100 for every municipality in the country.

title: ‘It brought kids back to canteens’: Lithuanian schools source food directly from farmers
snippet: Schools are choosing to prepare meals themselves rather than buy catering services, aiming to ensure children receive fresh, high-quality food in their canteens. They are adopting a short food supply chain model, buying vegetables, eggs and meat from local farmers.
